speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Down syndrome with associated duodenal atresia. The clinical presentation of bilious vomiting in a newborn with classic dysmorphic features (upslanting palpebral fissures, low-set ears, single transverse palmar crease) and a holosystolic murmur is highly suggestive of this diagnosis, which carries a significant risk for duodenal atresia. While the bilious nature of the vomiting can sometimes suggest distal obstruction like malrotation, duodenal atresia is the most critical diagnosis to confirm given the strong genetic syndrome and the potential "double bubble" sign on the abdominal X-ray. Immediate surgical consultation is required to evaluate for atresia or malrotation with midgut volvulus.
